## Core Question

Did the spatial concentration of LAPD policing activity in Black and Latino neighborhoods change after the discontinuation of PredPol in April 2020 — and does any change (or lack of change) persist into 2022–2024, past any plausible lagged effect of the algorithm?

## Why This Question

LAPD used PredPol, a place-based predictive policing algorithm, from roughly 2011 until April 2020, when Chief Michel Moore suspended the program under scrutiny over racial bias. The algorithm predicted crime at the block-group level and directed patrol resources accordingly.

Two interpretations of PredPol's spatial effects are possible:

- **Algorithm-as-driver**: PredPol independently concentrated policing in certain neighborhoods beyond what existing patrol patterns would have produced. Under this view, removing the algorithm should shift spatial distributions.
- **Algorithm-as-encoder**: PredPol encoded pre-existing patrol biases. Under this view, spatial concentration should persist after removal because the underlying deployment logic didn't change.

The before/after structure of LAPD's public data allows a descriptive test of which pattern is more consistent with the evidence.

## What Has Already Been Done

The obvious version of this project — disparate impact analysis of PredPol predictions at the census block group level — was done by [The Markup in 2021](https://themarkup.org/show-your-work/2021/12/02/how-we-determined-crime-prediction-software-disproportionately-targeted-low-income-black-and-latino-neighborhoods). [DaViera (2024)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ajcp.12671) analyzed the Strategic Subject List (a person-based tool) using CRT framework. Both are pre-discontinuation or tool-specific.

The post-PredPol era (2022–2024) spatial distribution of policing under the current regime is less studied. That's the gap.

## Data

All public via [data.lacity.org](https://data.lacity.org):

- LAPD Crime Incidents (geocoded, 2010–2024)
- LAPD Arrest data
- ACS 5-year estimates for tract-level demographics (race, poverty, income) via `tidycensus`

Unit of analysis: census tract or LAPD division (TBD based on data granularity).

## Analytical Structure

Three time periods:

| Period                 | Years     | Label               |
|------------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Pre-PredPol suspension | 2015–2019 | Pre                 |
| Transition / COVID     | 2020–2021 | Excluded or dummied |
| Post-PredPol           | 2022–2024 | Post                |

The COVID/transition period is handled by either dropping 2020–2021 entirely or including a binary dummy — this separates any distributional change from pandemic-era shifts in crime and patrol patterns. Patterns that persist through 2022–2024 cannot plausibly be attributed to PredPol's lagged effects.

## Outcome Variable Options

Three possible operationalizations, in increasing analytical interest:

1.  Arrest rate by tract (what police did)
2.  Reported crime rate by tract (what victims reported)
3.  **Ratio of arrests to reported crime** — a proxy for over-policing; tracts where arrests exceed what reported crime would predict

The third is the most interesting and least saturated in existing work.

## Primary Output

Before/after choropleth maps showing spatial concentration of policing activity overlaid with race and poverty — directly satisfies CLO3 (choropleth maps) and CLO9 (complete research project on an urban issue). LA's heterogeneity is an asset here: the variation across neighborhoods is what makes the maps meaningful.

## Why LA Works for This

LA's demographic heterogeneity, which makes it a bad choice for many projects, is an asset here. Stark spatial variation in race and income across the city means the maps do real analytical work rather than just decoration.

## Key Limitation

This is descriptive, not causal. Even a clean before/after shift cannot be attributed to PredPol's removal — other factors (department policy changes, budget, political pressure) also changed around 2020. The claim is interpretive, not causal, and needs to be framed accordingly.
